methods: record(entityType, entityId, action, performedBy, oldValues, newValues)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: Audit + Shared Infrastructure
recommended_phases.rationale: Audit has zero module dependencies and is required by every other module (GP-002). Build it first along with the shared DB connection and base repository. This unlocks all downstream modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Employee + Policy modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee and Policy each depend only on Audit (already built). They are independent of each other and can be built in parallel. Employee provides identity/manager lookups; Policy provides leave-type rules and entitlements.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Balance depends on Employee, Policy, and Audit — all built in Phases 1–2. It owns leave-balance tracking, deduction, restoration, and sufficiency checks. Must exist before Leave can deduct/restore balances.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Notification depends only on Audit. It can be built in parallel with Phase 3. Provides the notification fanout that Leave will trigger on state transitions.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Leave module (orchestrator)
recommended_phases.rationale: Leave depends on all other modules: Employee (identity/manager), Policy (rule validation), Balance (deduction/restoration), Audit (GP-002), Notification (state-change alerts). It orchestrates the full leave-request lifecycle: submit → approve/reject/cancel. This is the largest module and the integration point.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes/controllers in leave module only), application (service interfaces + implementations across all modules), domain (models/enums in each module), infrastructure (repositories in each module, shared DB connection). Dependencies flow strictly inward: leave → {balance, employee, policy, notification, audit}; balance → {employee, policy, audit}; employee → {audit}; policy → {audit}; notification → {audit}; audit → none. No circular dependencies exist. Every state-changing operation in LeaveService writes an audit record (GP-002) and triggers notifications. Balance deductions happen atomically within approveLeaveRequest; restorations on cancel/reject. RBAC enforcement (GP-005) is applied at the route/controller layer in the leave module — not in the service interface itself, keeping the service layer role-agnostic.
